hints.content:
The basic function $\cos(x)$ has a maximum point at $(0,1)$ and intersects its midline at $\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2},0\right)$.

$\qquad$![](${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/7e259eb428a1b2f16d2104452d48ea61.png)

Let's transform $\pink{\cos(x)}$ to $\blue{4\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}x+\pi\right)-3}$ step by step and see how the graph changes along the way.

The transformation from $\pink{\cos(x)}$ to $\green{\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}x\right)}$ is a horizontal shrink by a factor of $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$, so the intersection point's horizontal distance from the origin is shrunk from $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ to $\dfrac{\pi}{2}\cdot\dfrac{3}{\pi}=1.5$.

$\qquad$[[☃ image 1]]

The transformation from $\green{\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}x\right)}$ to $\red{4\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}x\right)}$ is a vertical stretch by a factor of $4$, so the maximum point's vertical distance from the origin is stretched from $1$ to $4$.

$\qquad$[[☃ image 2]]

options.alt: A dashed graph and a solid graph trigonometric wave on an x y coordinate plane. The x axis scales by one and the y axis scales by one. On the dashed graph there is a point on the graph at a maximum at (zero, one) and a point on the midline next to the mentioned point at (pi over two, zero). On the solid graph, there is a point on the graph at a maximum at (zero, one) and a point at the midline next to the mentioned point around (one and one half, zero).

A dashed graph and a solid graph trigonometric wave on an x y coordinate plane. The x axis scales by one and the y axis scales by one. On the dashed graph there is a point on the graph at a maximum at (zero, one) and a point at the midline next to the mentioned point around (one and one half, zero). On the solid graph, there is a point on the graph at a maximum at (zero, four) and a point at the midline next to the mentioned point around (one and one half, zero).

hints.content: The transformation from $\red{4\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}x\right)}$ to $\blue{4\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}x+\pi\right)-3}$, which is equivalent to $4\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}(x+3)\right)-3$, is a translation to the left by $3$ units and a translation downwards by $3$ units.

As a result of these transformations, the maximum point is now at $\left(-3,1\right)$ and the intersection with the midline is at $(-1.5,-3)$.

The resulting graph looks as follows:

$\qquad$[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A graph of a trigonometric wave on an x y coordinate plane. The x axis scales by one and the y axis scales by one. There is a point on the graph at a maximum at (negative three, one) and a point on the midline next to the mentioned point at (negative one and one half, negative three).

*Note that one moveable point always defines an extremum point in the graph and the other point always defines a neighbouring intersection with the midline.*
